stem: The expression \((2x + 5)^{2} - (2x - 5)^{2}\) is equivalent to \(kx\), where \(k\) is a constant. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Use the difference of squares \(A^{2} - B^{2} = (A + B)(A - B)\) with \(A = 2x + 5\) and \(B = 2x - 5\).
\(A + B = 4x\) and \(A - B = 10\), so the expression is \(4x \cdot 10 = 40x\).
So \(k = 40\). (Expanding both squares gives the same result: \(4x^{2} + 20x + 25 - (4x^{2} - 20x + 25) = 40x\).)
verify:
x = symbols('x')
e = expand((2*x + 5)**2 - (2*x - 5)**2)
assert e == 40*x
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [40]
